detailedDerivation: For a positive parent maximizer, D−E=b_(j+1), D+E+K=2b_j+b_(j−1), so S=K+2E. Also D=(T−K+b_(j+1))/2≥b_j−K/2.
Integer D therefore contains the selected m=max(0,ceil(ωb_j−K/2)) sources for0<ω≤1. A predeclared fibre≤C map into the actual extra-owner tails yields m≤CE, so CE+K/2≥ωb_j.
For C≥1, S=K+2E≥2ωb_j/C. If b_(j+1)=0, S=T≥2b_j and the same conclusion holds without a response map.

Active b_j>0 are integer, so division by max(1,b_j) is division by b_j. Clipping at2 still leavesδ≥2ω/C. Divergent predeclared active weight therefore supplies the cumulative-transfer hypothesis; the even lane’s transfer plus fixed-window tiling gives J=o(N).

When K=0, triple(b,b,−e) with e=ωb/C saturates the coefficient, establishing inventory-level sharpness. Scale tagging allows repeated absolute days across scales but requires actual tail incidence per scale; arbitrary membership or postselected weights cannot be substituted.
